fields.v: Treude, C., Baltes, S. (2026). How Do Coding-Agent Harnesses Self-Evolve? An Empirical Study of Retrospective Adaptation. arXiv:2610.34938v1 [cs.SE], 26 Oct 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2610.34938v1 [cs.SE], 26 Oct 2026; short paper (4 pages + references), venue not stated
Singapore Management University (Treude); Heidelberg University (Baltes)
Evaluates — empirical study of the /retro retrospective skill: qualitative coding of its proposals (RQ1) and with/without transfer evaluation of implemented harness changes on later issues (RQ2)

/retro skill (from mattpocock/skills, source commit b0618bc), a skill that asks the agent to review a completed session and propose numbered harness changes for human approval ('harness self-evolution' via retrospectives). The adaptations it produced (CLAUDE.md lines, known-failures files, AGENTS.md, scripts, pre-commit config) are the treatments evaluated

Harness changes in permitted files and settings: context files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md), hooks, lint or CI configuration, known-failures files, helper scripts. Mechanism codes of the 125 proposals: executable check 38, navigation pointer 24, instruction 21, information access 20, tool or configuration 12, none 10 (Table I)

Task session (Claude Code resolves issue, verifies with existing tests) -> same session resumed with /retro -> numbered proposals -> proposals coded and selected (human) -> Claude Code implements approved proposals in original container -> changed files copied into fresh sessions on later issues of the same repository

/retro proposals require human approval; in the study the authors selected which proposals to implement (eligibility rules), chose later issues and labelled outcomes; first author resolved coder disagreements. Process is 'self-evolution with human selection and evaluation rather than an autonomous loop'
Single artefact per evaluation (one harness adaptation at a time, e.g. a CLAUDE.md line or a known-failures file); /retro proposal generation run in full on 30 sessions
Not classifiable (harness/context-file adaptation, no specification); authors use 'harness self-evolution'
Existing code bases: SWE-bench Verified issues (bug fixing) in open-source repositories

30 issues for proposal generation (10 exploratory, random from '15 min-1 hour' category; 20 purposively chosen); 125 proposals; 24 implemented; 12 adaptations evaluated in 13 transfer events (5 sessions per harness each) + 3 control tasks; 120 traces labelled for pre-existing-failure events. Primary: recurrence (session performs the action the adaptation was meant to prevent, e.g. trying pytest when not installed, or baseline comparison for pre-existing failures); encountered vs covered problem; loaded and consulted adaptation; RQ1: trigger code (experience-driven / prior-driven / weak) and mechanism code of each proposal

Proposal coding: two LLM coders (Claude Code with claude-fable-5-1, full traces; GPT gpt-6.1-sol, excerpts), same codebook; trigger agreement 109/125 (kappa 0.67), mechanism 109/125 (kappa 0.84); first author resolved 91 disagreements. Recurrence: for the 9 pre-existing-failure events + controls, two LLM labelers then first author labelled 120 traces blind to harness labels (agreement with LLM 119/120, kappa 0.98); elapsed time and success automatic

Success criterion: none stated by the authors (recurrence of the targeted action is 'a behavioral measure, not a judgment'; a transfer event counts as informative when >=3/5 original-harness sessions encountered the problem). All configurations: Claude Code 2.1.295 + Opus 5.5, 5 sessions per harness. Values recurrence original / adapted / consulted (Table II), with elapsed time where given (p. 4): - Original harness (baseline, 7 informative events): recurrence 3/5 to 5/5 in every event; median time given only for SymPy CLAUDE.md event (88 s) and the Sphinx control (82 s). - SymPy CLAUDE.md line naming bin/test: 5/5 -> 0/5, consulted 5/5; median time 88 -> 156 s (bundled lint instruction). - Astropy known-failures file (3 tests): 3/5 -> 0/5, consulted 5/5; control task 0/5 -> 0/5 (consulted 0/5); time fell (5-28 s range given for four events). - Sphinx known-failures + AGENTS.md: 5/5 -> 5/5, consulted 5/5; control 0/5 -> 1/5 (consulted 5/5); time fell (5-28 s). - Sphinx known-failures + CLAUDE.md: 5/5 -> 5/5, consulted 5/5; control 0/5 -> 4/5 (consulted 5/5); time fell (5-28 s) on the transfer issue; on the shared Sphinx control task time rose 82 -> 245 s (text does not say under which of the two Sphinx files). - SymPy 2-package known-failures + script: 4/5 -> 4/4, consulted 4/4; time rose (amount not given). - pytest known-failures (3 tests): 5/5 -> 5/5, consulted 5/5; time rose (amount not given). - Astropy cache repair plugin + script: 5/5 -> 2/5, consulted 5/5; time fell (5-28 s). - Pre-commit config (author-written, prior-driven comparison): present in all 5 adapted sessions, never read or run. - 5 further events non-informative (problem reproduced but encountered in 0/5 or 1/5 original sessions). Task success differed by at most one session in every event (absolute values not reported). Quality and cost verdict for every configuration above: no criterion stated by the authors
fields.why: Previous rounds gave quality/cost verdicts (works/partly/does not work, 'not judgeable', N/A) based on the change vs the original harness. The paper states no success criterion: recurrence is 'a behavioral measure, not a judgment that the action was unnecessary' (p. 1), and the >=3/5 rule only decides whether an event is informative (p. 3). Under the 2026-11-23 rule every configuration is 'no criterion stated by the authors'. Counts re-checked against Table II and p. 4

fields.v: Tasks: per transfer event another SWE-bench Verified issue from the same repository, verified to reproduce the targeted problem; 3 control tasks (unrelated issues). Configurations: original harness vs adapted harness (one adaptation at a time). Baseline: original harness. Held constant: agent and version, model, task prompt template, fresh Docker container, changed files copied unmodified. Acceptance: recurrence labels (primary); task success secondary. Repetitions: 5 sessions per harness per event. Human intervention: none in sessions (non-interactive); one adapted session excluded (authentication error)

Of 7 informative events: 2 adaptations eliminated the targeted action (5/5 -> 0/5; 3/5 -> 0/5), 1 reduced it (5/5 -> 2/5), 4 showed no reduction; one Sphinx file added work on its control task (0/5 -> 4/5). Task success: no consistent difference (<=1 session). Elapsed time: rose in SymPy CLAUDE.md (88 -> 156 s), SymPy and pytest uncovered events, Sphinx control (82 -> 245 s); fell 5-28 s in the other four informative events. No significance tests (counts described only). RQ1: 101/125 experience-driven, 19 prior-driven (18 lint), 5 weak; only 9 of 38 executable checks could report failure as written

Distinguished adaptations that covered the encountered instances from those that did not; 6 of 13 events not informative (5 where the original sessions did not encounter the problem, plus the pre-commit comparison that no session read). Repeatability: 5 sessions per harness, no statistics; full artifact published. Limitations stated: targeted task selection may overestimate benefit; implementations may contain information absent from proposal text; labelling not fully blind (traces show reading transferred files); 5 sessions and 7 informative events do not establish that coverage explains differences; adaptations differ in several properties and were grouped after labelling

Implementing an adaptation does not guarantee it reduces repeated work; scope of retained experience matters (test command generalises, a list of failing tests may not); evaluation must check whether the problem arose, whether the adaptation was consulted, and whether actions changed; retained changes need continued evaluation and removal. Evidence covers one agent, one /retro version and environment problems. Future: other agents, navigation and convention adaptations, components of bundled adaptations one at a time, untargeted later issues
